source_contract: Three LCB clients retain functional argument expansion, persistent function state, stdin capture, source numeric/list coercion and difficulty/repetition metrics. CodeElo/CodeForces retain their canonical stdin-only contracts, reference trailing-marker cleanup, exact output equality and source main-guard behavior. Candidate-only RPC runs programs without trusted test answers; ScriptSpec supervisor compares data returns.
execution_bounds: LCB retains six-second per-test and thirty-second whole-run budgets. CodeElo uses source milliseconds and (timeout+1)*tests+5 seconds; CodeForces uses source seconds and (timeout+1)*tests+60. Legacy source has no per-test alarm. LCB retains 1 GiB AS/DATA/STACK limits in the candidate worker plus a 1 GiB Docker memory limit. Legacy profiles inherit the execution environment limit, matching their uncapped source. Older RPC callers retain the 256 MiB Docker default. Process-group and container cleanup run on timeout.
scoring_fixes: LCB integer-list coercion previously awarded [1.9] against [1.1]; lossless coercion remains but truncation no longer earns credit. Canonical fractional lists still match.

Empty/malformed tests, missing configured repetitions and invalid trusted metadata abort batches. Infrastructure errors propagate through source thread collection instead of becoming partial aggregate metrics.
limitations: Fixture-only actual evaluate_responses methods; source parsing has_code produces fixture model_answers. No model inference, dataset loading or archived-score replay claimed.

Candidate runtime is the existing pinned Python/numpy image. Baseline original scorers execute on macOS; Linux source resource-limit behavior is separately exercised with ordinary allocation regressions.
Source APIs and comparison helpers are pinned; arbitrary source future versions or external candidate libraries are outside this evidence.
